source_text: Sed ais me noluisse concupiscentiam carnis nominare. Qui nolui nominare, tacui; et si tacui, nihil quod reprehenderes sum locutus: quis ergo errorem persuadet tacendo? O nova criminum et hactenus inaudita portenta! Silentio meo ait perversum dogma componi!
pass_a_gloss: But you say that I was unwilling to name the desire of the flesh. He who was unwilling to name, was silent; and if I was silent, I have spoken nothing that you might blame: who therefore persuades error by being silent? O new portents of charges and until now unheard! He says that a perverse dogma is composed by my silence!

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae

pass_b_english: Instead you say I was unwilling to name the desire of the flesh. If I was unwilling to name it, I kept silent; and if I kept silent, I said nothing for you to criticize. Who, then, persuades someone to adopt an error by keeping silent? What new and previously unheard-of monstrosities of accusation! He says a perverse doctrine is being constructed out of my silence!

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
